label: Travel referral program, 80 partners
note: A clean export with one partner at about 27% of revenue. A correct reading is moderate risk: the top 3 partners bring in about 48% and you need 4 partners to reach half of revenue.

label: Fundraising partners, European export
note: Semicolons, decimal commas, euro signs, a refund in brackets, a blank partner and a "Total" row. Pick the columns by hand and clean those rows first; after cleaning there are 9 partners and the biggest holds about 45% of revenue, which is high risk.

label: Nine sub-IDs of one network
note: Nine partner IDs that all belong to one parent network, each near 9%. Looked at one by one the risk seems low, but grouped by parent one network holds about 79% of revenue.

label: Five equal partners
note: Five partners with 20% each. Perfectly even sharing in a small program still scores as moderate risk because the score has a built-in floor, so do not read it as a warning.

label: Three equal partners
note: Three partners with a third each. A "high risk" label here only reflects that there are few partners, not that one of them dominates.

label: Exactly 80% in two partners
note: Shares of 70, 10, 10 and 10 percent. The correct answer is that 2 partners reach 80% of revenue, so a result of 3 partners is a rounding error.

label: Partner with negative net revenue
note: One partner has refunds larger than sales. A careful reading includes that reversal in the total instead of dropping the partner.

label: One partner has all the revenue
note: A single partner earns everything. The right answer is 100% concentrated, not an error message.

label: Title lines above the header
note: An export with report title lines before the column names. Delete the lines above the header row and upload again if the columns are not found.

label: Tab-separated file
note: The same kind of data with tabs instead of commas. It should load normally.
